theme.title: Beyond the Box Score
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: Against the Knicks in 1995, Reggie Miller scored how many points in 8.9 seconds?
questions.context: 1995 East semifinals · Game 1 · at New York

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: scored eight unanswered points in 8.9 seconds in Game 1

funFacts.text: The comeback featured a stolen inbounds pass from Anthony Mason between Miller's dramatic jumpers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: stole the inbound pass from Anthony Mason

funFacts.text: John Starks missed both free throws on New York's next possession, leaving the door open for Indiana.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Starks missed both free throws

funFacts.text: Patrick Ewing grabbed the offensive rebound but his putback bounced off the back rim.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: his shot was just a bit long and hit the back rim

questions.prompt: The 1966–67 Sixers averaged 125 points. Before the shot clock, Fort Wayne beat Minneapolis in 1950 with how many?
questions.context: Fort Wayne Pistons vs Minneapolis Lakers · November 22, 1950

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: defeated the Minneapolis Lakers by a record-low score of 19–18, including 3–1 in the fourth quarter.

funFacts.text: Fort Wayne attempted just 13 field goals during the entire low-scoring game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they attempted 13 shots for the game

funFacts.text: The slow-down strategy was designed to keep the ball away from Lakers giant George Mikan.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: to limit the impact of the Lakers' dominant George Mikan

funFacts.text: A St. Paul newspaper condemned the Pistons' tactic as a black eye for pro basketball.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: gave pro basketball a great black eye

questions.prompt: David West averaged 20.6 next to Chris Paul in 2007–08. What did Mo Williams average beside LeBron in his first Cavaliers season?
questions.note: 17.8 points per game as LeBron's new backcourt partner.

funFacts.text: Williams made 43.6% of his three-pointers that season, while shooting 91.2% at the line.
Cleveland acquired Williams from Milwaukee in a three-team trade during the offseason.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: To Milwaukee Bucks----Damon Jones----To Oklahoma City Thunder----Joe Smith | To Cleveland Cavaliers----Mo Williams

funFacts.text: Williams posted a season-high 44 points against Phoenix in February.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: February 11 Phoenix W 109–92 Maurice Williams (44)

questions.prompt: On Michael Jordan's famous 'Last Shot' against Utah in the 1998 Finals, how many seconds remained after the ball went in?
questions.context: Michael Jordan · Bulls at Jazz · 1998 Finals Game 6
questions.note: 5.2 seconds. Jordan's jumper helped clinch Chicago's sixth title in eight seasons.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jordan then hit a 20-footer to give the Bulls an 87–86 lead with 5.2 seconds left.

funFacts.text: Jordan stole the ball from Karl Malone just before the shot.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jordan stole the ball from Karl Malone in the low post and dribbled down the court.

funFacts.text: John Stockton missed Utah's final chance to win it.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: John Stockton took the inbound pass, and missed a game-winning 3-pointer

funFacts.text: Jordan finished the deciding game with 45 points.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Michael Jordan took 35 of the Bulls' 67 shots, leading the team in scoring and minutes played with 45 points
